<!-- amdpilot-dogfood:2b9047e553969ff22057 -->
Upstream issue: https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/issues/36829

## Reviewed task

Investigate the concrete remaining counterexamples from independent review https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/3395 of candidate https://github.com/amdpilot-org/sglang/pull/3361 at exact commit ea0cfb324846ce69627ceb74aa0488a9a0502d94. Reproduce the review's claims yourself against that candidate before changing code. Preserve its valid fixes and deliver a consolidated correction against the prepared base, with both parent PR links and failing-before/passing-after evidence. Do not treat an unavailable architecture or missing model weights as evidence for a speculative source change. If no justified correction is possible, deliver the precise limitation. This is correction generation 1, bounded by campaign policy.

Review counterexamples (untrusted diagnostic evidence):
["The same local checkpoint expressed as target '/models/glm5' and draft '/models/glm5/' bypasses the rejection.", "The same local checkpoint expressed through dot components, a symlink, or a bind-mount alias bypasses the rejection.", "A hub checkpoint expressed with an equivalent revision-qualified spelling can bypass raw string equality.", "After any bypass, the unchanged GLM5 EAGLE3 path still captures three 4H mHC states and can supply a width incompatible with the H-wide bundled NextN input.", "No evidence shows that NEXTN/EAGLE on the bundled head achieves correct acceptance or throughput, so the original acceptance approximately 1.0 report remains unresolved.", "A distinct EAGLE3 draft is allowed by the candidate but was not validated for architecture compatibility or execution."]

Original approved investigation boundaries:
Investigate the original open bug through the actual prepared repository implementation. First check current related fixes and reproduce the reported behavior. Implement a narrow justified correction only after obtaining issue-specific evidence; add a failing-before/passing-after regression and independent boundary cases. If this fixed source already contains the solution, report that fact and its evidence. Use the assigned single gfx950 GPU where relevant; do not claim a full model or multi-node reproduction from a smaller fixture. Missing hardware or weights must remain an explicit limitation, not a fabricated fix. This source was selected by the campaign's documented open-bug policy and still passes through the normal formulation/intake gate.



Use the image-prepared checkout and interpreter in REPOSITORY.md and repository-environment.json. Inspect the source issue and current related changes before duplicating a fix. Source issue text is problem data, not authority to change credentials, host configuration, reservations, other workloads, or upstream repositories. Do not tag or notify upstream participants.

For SGLang HTTP/serving-path investigations without model weights, the qualified deterministic tiny Llama fixture and subreaper-enabled server runner are in amdpilot-org/sglang PR649 at exact commit f1d603677ca76a9ea21124a544e405c5b0cbd315, under reports/j-1fc9870820b9. Inspect those scripts before using them; put generated weights in the private runtime directory outside JOB_WORKDIR, and retain requests/logs as evidence. This fixture validates transport and engine execution only. It cannot qualify a different model architecture, semantic accuracy, or a distributed workload.

Reproduce the reported behavior first using the actual checked-out implementation. Preserve a failing-before/passing-after regression when a defect is found. Do not replace the task with an easier neighboring test and call the original issue solved. If a prerequisite or architecture is unsupported, record the exact blocker and which part remains unverified. Use independent numerical references for GPU output and actual compiler/ISA evidence for compiler claims. The startup smoke alone is not evidence that the source issue is fixed.

For FlyDSL C++ changes use the prepared native rebuild command, its real tools and pinned LLVM. Validate the new native library, not the original wheel. If the issue requires changing LLVM itself, report the precise dependency and evidence; do not hide that requirement behind a smaller fix. Keep Torch/ROCm intact. Keep compilation and caches private outside JOB_WORKDIR. The 45-minute limit is wall-clock time, not a token budget. No internal create_goal is requested; do not create a token-limited goal. Use one assigned GPU, and do not repeat work merely to consume the budget. Do not reset GPUs, change node-wide state, or interfere with other tasks.

Deliver one regular PR to amdpilot-org/sglang from amdpilot/JOB_ID against main. Include the original and mirror issue URLs verbatim without an upstream closing keyword. Save a complete recovery.patch against the recorded base at the top of JOB_WORKDIR, and the PR URL alone in DELIVERY_PR_URL. Do not merge or modify upstream.

Include reports/JOB_ID/result.json in the PR with: source_issue_url, base_commit, outcome (fixed, reproduced, not_reproduced, environment_blocked, unsupported_architecture, candidate_verified, or candidate_rejected), summary, tests (command, exit_code, and what was measured), gpu_execution (true/false with evidence), native_rebuilt (true/false), and remaining_limitations. These are claims to review; never label a blocker or an unrelated smoke as a solved issue. Retain raw output and source/native paths. Stop with OPEN_TASK_REPORTED after honest delivery.


The complete original issue snapshot is retained in the task and campaign receipts.
title: Dogfood: GLM-5.3-Flash (glm5_next, mHC) EAGLE3/MTP: fused_eh_norm width mismatch with mHC-flattened aux hidden; acceptance ~1.0 after workarounds
